summary: Records that, following RFC 9280, responsibility for the RFC Series moved from the RFC Editor to the RFC Series Working Group and the RFC Series Approval Board, and the IAB's role changed. It does this by deleting a sentence from Section 2.1 of RFC 2026 saying RFC publication is the direct responsibility of the RFC Editor. It is a Best Current Practice.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice updates RFC 2026 after the RFC Series responsibility model changed. It deletes one sentence that assigned RFC publication directly to the RFC Editor.

subtitle: A Best Current Practice deletes an outdated responsibility statement from RFC 2026.

tldr.problem: RFC 2026 still assigned direct responsibility for RFC publication to the RFC Editor under the IAB, while RFC 9280 changed the RFC Series model.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9282 deletes that sentence from Section 2.1 of RFC 2026.
tldr.outcome: The RFC 2026 text is aligned with the responsibility change described in RFC 9280. RFC 9282 has no IANA actions and presents no security considerations.

today: RFC 9282 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 2026 to reflect RFC 9280. The unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes RFC 9282.

sections.title: The Responsibility Change
sections.content:
RFC 9280 moved responsibility for the RFC Series to the RFC Series Working Group and the RFC Series Approval Board. The RFC Editor is no longer responsible for the series in the way described by the old text, and the IAB's role changed.

RFC 9282 updates Section 2.1 of RFC 2026 to reflect that change.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC Series model changed, so an older sentence about responsibility was no longer accurate. This RFC removes that sentence.

sections.title: The Sentence Removed
sections.content:
RFC 9282 deletes the sentence in Section 2.1 of RFC 2026 that says RFC publication is the direct responsibility of the RFC Editor under the general direction of the IAB.

The document does not provide replacement wording.
sections.plainLanguage: The old sentence assigning direct responsibility for publication is removed. The RFC does not add a replacement sentence.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC has no IANA actions and presents no security considerations. It changes only the responsibility sentence in Section 2.1 of RFC 2026.
sections.plainLanguage: This change to an organizational statement requires no IANA action and presents no security considerations.
